elaine_sales: Hey team — presales ask from an EU bank POC. They need: (1) a simple data residency statement we can commit to for the POC, (2) a one-page data flow diagram showing boundaries and subprocessors, and (3) if doing Dedicated/Private will change pricing. Can someone own this? Need to respond by EOD tomorrow.

marco_eng: I can draft the diagram. Quick clarifying Qs: is the POC going into their VPC (private deployment) or do they want Redwood-hosted in eu-west? That changes what subprocessors we list and whether we can commit to KMS BYOK.

elaine_sales: They said "prefer private VPC" but will accept hosted if we provide guarantees. Also asked whether logs or telemetry might leave EU during debugging.

marco_eng: Short answer: for Private (customer VPC) we can keep all inference traffic inside their VPC and only the control plane metadata may talk to Redwood control plane (we can restrict control plane egress to EU regions). For Hosted (Redwood-managed) data at-rest and in-transit are encrypted; metadata and tracing may hit our control plane in the region. We can provide a diagram like below and a checklist for what we can guarantee.

marco_eng: ```
Client (EU VPC) -> Private Connector -> Dedicated GW (eu-west1) -> Redwood Inference (dedicated pool)
- KV cache and model weights pinned to eu-west1 GPUs
- Customer KMS: optional BYOK (only metadata handshake goes to Redwood control-plane)
- Logs: application logs kept in eu-west S3 bucket; debug traces redacted unless customer opts-in
```

alyssa_legal: A few legal/security constraints: we can provide an EU-only data residency statement for the POC if they choose Private or Dedicated in eu-west1. For Hosted we can provide "data residency in EU" but cannot guarantee that all support/debug traces remain in EU unless they sign the support scoping addendum. Also: we cannot share raw KMS keys or private key material — we can confirm KMS provider, region, and whether HSM-backed keys are used.

mike_se: Pricing notes: Dedicated reserved capacity has a setup delta and minimum monthly commit. For a POC (2–4 concurrent slots, short 4-week run) we usually propose a temporary dedicated pool with a pro-rated setup fee ~ $Xk + usage. Private (customer-hosted) has SKU for private control plane + per-GPU cost; it's typically higher ops effort. Hosted is cheapest but less isolation. I can put numbers together if we know expected qps and sequence lengths.

elaine_sales: Customer asked for the subprocessor list (to feed vendor risk). Can we give them a redacted subprocessor list and an export they can use for their vendor intake team?

alyssa_legal: Yes — we have an approved subprocessor export template (we redact contract-level pricing, but list provider name, region, subproc role (storage, telemetry, infra), and SOC attestations). We also have a standard CAIQ/SIG mapping pack. I can attach the template and a note about notification windows (we notify customers 30 days before adding a critical subprocessor unless contractually agreed otherwise).

marco_eng: Action items I can take: (A) produce a one-page dataflow diagram (SVG + PNG) showing control-plane vs data-plane, KMS boundaries, and redactable subprocessor pins; (B) provide the minimal config snippet for private connector. Target: draft by 09:00 UTC tomorrow. Anyone else take pricing/contract ownership?

mike_se: I'll sketch the POC pricing options and put three scenarios (Hosted minimal, Dedicated short-term, Private on-customer infra) with ballpark numbers. ETA EOD today.

elaine_sales: Great—please cc me when you drop artifacts. Also need a sentence we can paste into the customer's vendor portal: "Redwood will keep all inference inputs and outputs stored in the customer's EU region for the duration of the POC; debug traces are disabled by default and will not be exported outside the EU unless explicitly enabled under a support engagement." Is that acceptable?

alyssa_legal: That phrasing is OK if the customer chooses Private/Dedicated in the EU region. For Hosted we should change to "we store customer POC data in EU regions by default; certain control-plane metadata may be processed outside the EU; see support addendum for stricter guarantees." I'll provide both canned statements.

elaine_sales: Perfect. Any blockers from SRE/infra about delivering the diagram or evidence? If not I'll respond to the customer and ask for confirmation of VPC vs hosted.

deploy-bot: uploaded: redwood-subprocessors-export-template_v3.pdf (shared to channel)

marco_eng: I have one technical caveat to note in the diagram re: cache eviction and model shards — if they want strict EU residency we must ensure the cache persistence tier is in eu-west; otherwise some ephemeral shards could be pulled from regional cache nodes. I'll annotate the diagram.

mike_se: FYI — if they request BYOK + HSM-backed keys, onboarding time increases (legal + key exchange) and we typically add a 2-week lead time. Calling that out in the proposal will manage expectations.

elaine_sales: Awesome. Plan: I will email the customer now asking them to confirm "Private VPC" vs "Redwood-hosted in EU" by EOD; Marco will draft diagram by 09:00 UTC tomorrow; Mike will post pricing options EOD today; Alyssa will attach subprocessor export + canned statements. Thanks all :thumbsup:

alyssa_legal: Adding note — if they need the subprocessor list with contact-level SOC details we need a signed NDA. Will attach the standard NDA template if requested.

marco_eng: Noted. I'll keep the diagram minimal and mark any fields that require legal signoff.

elaine_sales: Sending the customer reply now. I'll include the expected deliverable deadlines and loop back here when they reply.
